confidence_explanation: The evidence clearly shows a mid-session IP change for user_10, followed by a pattern of accessing and downloading sensitive files from departments outside their authorized scope (HR, Legal, DevOps runbooks) during off-hours.

attack_chain.description: User_10 logs in successfully from their normal IP (192.168.1.110) within normal hours.
Session hijacking occurs: the same session_id (sess_user_10_20260630_001) is used from a new, external IP (176.10.99.200) during off-hours.
Attacker begins unauthorized cross-department access, downloading sensitive HR files.
Attacker performs bulk downloads of DevOps runbooks and other sensitive files (Legal, HR) across multiple departments.
Attacker logs out after successful data exfiltration.

gaps: Geographic location of IP 176.10.99.200 to confirm it is not a known VPN used by the user.
Logs from the endpoint of user_10 to determine if the session was hijacked via malware or if the user's credentials were stolen.
narrative: A session hijacking incident occurred involving user_10. After an initial legitimate login, the session was hijacked by an external IP (176.10.99.200), which then performed a bulk download of sensitive files from the HR, Legal, and DevOps departments, all of which are outside the user's authorized directory scope.
